title: Dominik Szoboszlai apologises to Liverpool fans for ‘misunderstanding’ during Manchester City defeat
content:
Dominik Szoboszlai has apologised to Liverpool supporters for his reaction following the club’s recent FA Cup defeat to Manchester City.

The Hungary midfielder was criticised for throwing his arms up in frustration in front of the away fans who had stayed until the end of the dismal 4-0 defeat at the Etihad Stadium.

Szoboszlai, who has previously bemoaned the sight of supporters leaving games early at Anfield, stood accused of being out of touch given the paucity of the performance served up by Arne Slot’s side.

“Yeah to make it clear, maybe it was a misunderstanding between me and the fans,” he told reporters at a press conference at Anfield to preview Tuesday’s Champions League quarter-final second leg with Paris Saint-Germain.

“I didn’t mean it in a bad way. I know what the fans mean for this club and what this club means to the fans. As a player we do everything for them as well as for ourselves. So if it was a misunderstanding then I apologise.

“They can feel also that I am not feeling better than them. I am feeling exactly the same way like they do. I want to make it clear I am with them, we are with them and hopefully they are with us as well.”

Szoboszlai has been Liverpool’s outstanding performer during a turbulent campaign and he delivered a bullish assessment of their chances of overturning a 2-0 deficit from last week’s first leg in Paris.

“I believe completely because I know what we are able to do, what kind of players we have and what kind of mentality we have. We’ve shown it many times, but maybe not every time, and that’s what we need again from the start,” he added.

“My message to the fans is that we are going to go all in. We’ll give our best from minute one to minute 90 or more if needed. We want it so bad.

“Anfield is going to make a big impact. We saw it many times before. It is going to be not only about 11 players or the subs, it is going to be the whole stadium. We know how it feels to be playing for Liverpool in front of these fans. We don’t need any more motivation.

“It is going to be a different game (compared to the first leg) for sure. We are going to do different stuff in a different way. If at the end you can say you gave everything and didn’t go through then you can still keep your chin up. To come from 2-0 down against Paris in the quarter-finals of the Champions League, it would be the biggest comeback in my career.”

Liverpool have scored two or more goals in 36 of their last 50 home matches in all competitions and Slot vowed his team will be “front-footed” as they attempt to knock Luis Enrique’s in-form side off their stride.

“Last week they had 76 per cent possession so that’s the first thing we have to change,” Slot said.

“We have to find the perfect balance between being offensive but doing the defensive job. We have to be much better than we were last week. The fans will be just as important as our performance. The atmosphere when we faced PSG here last season was unbelievable and I hope our fans can find an extra gear.”
